<PAGE><|det|>header [148, 53, 553, 67]<|/det|>shares = FullMath.mulDiv(num, total, denom);
<|det|>text [134, 98, 937, 184]<|/det|>It simply downscale the total amount of shares based on the provided value by the user and the total value. The issue is that cumulativeValue includes the deposit by the user which results in him receiving less shares as the total value is bigger.
<|det|>text [135, 203, 520, 223]<|/det|>Let's imagine the following scenario:
<|det|>text [133, 243, 900, 288]<|/det|>1. The preBalance of the token deposited is 10 and the added balance is also 10, thus tokenBalance is 20
<|det|>text [131, 310, 776, 330]<|/det|>2. We wrongly set cumulativeValue to tokenBalance or 20
<|det|>text [132, 352, 931, 395]<|/det|>3. We imagine that cumulative value is increased twice by 10 in the loop, to a total of 40
<|det|>text [131, 418, 881, 462]<|/det|>4. The shares for the user will be  \( 10 \times 100 / 40 = 25 \)  (assuming total shares are 100), the total shares go to 125 and the user shares are 25
<|det|>text [132, 483, 936, 552]<|/det|>5. If a user withdraws, he will be able to get 25 / 125 = 0.2 of the total value which we computed to be 40, thus 8 (2 less than what he deposited, he should get the same)
<|det|>text [135, 571, 938, 683]<|/det|>This is because cumulativeValue should be initialized with the value of preBalance[idx], that way the formula for the user shares will be 10 * 100 / 30 = 0.33 (30 comes from 10 tokens from the preBalance[idx] and 2 * 10 from the other tokens). Now, when the user withdraws, he will be able to get 33 / 133 = 0,2481203008 of the 40 assets which is ~10.
<|det|>title [105, 705, 425, 731]<|/det|>Recommendations
<|det|>text [135, 748, 531, 768]<|/det|>Modify LiqFacet::addLiq as follows:
<|det|>text [145, 796, 615, 842]<|/det|>- uint256 cumulativeValue = tokenBalance;
+ uint256 cumulativeValue = preBalance[idx];
<|det|>text [136, 870, 630, 890]<|/det|>Remove the following check in AssetLib::add:
<|det|>text [149, 920, 416, 936]<|/det|>require(num == denom, "NDE");
<|det|>page_number [486, 964, 511, 979]<|/det|>11
